1_hnswlib_builds_under_termux.evidence: hnswlib 0.8.0 compiles from source under Termux on aarch64 in 19 s with clang 21.1.8, producing hnswlib-0.8.0-cp314-cp314-android_24_arm64_v8a.whl. Toolchain: Python 3.14.6, numpy 2.4.4, pybind11 3.1.0, all from Termux's own repository.
1_hnswlib_builds_under_termux.why_it_matters: Upstream publishes no aarch64-android wheels and there is NO chroma-hnswlib fallback on this platform, unlike the Windows case (ADR-0017). It builds from source against clang or Phase 3.5 has no index on the device.
1_hnswlib_builds_under_termux.unblock: Run scripts/device_probe.sh in Termux; section 1 reports the build exit code, the last 25 lines of the compiler log, and a functional knn_query check rather than just an import.
1_hnswlib_builds_under_termux.the_finding: THE DEFAULT BUILD SUCCEEDS AND THE RESULT CRASHES. With hnswlib's normal flags the wheel builds cleanly, pip reports success, exit code 0 -- and `import hnswlib` dies with SIGILL (rc=132) before executing a single line. Every subsequent step fails identically, because none of them is reached. hnswlib's setup.py compiles with -march=native, and clang targeting this core emitted an instruction it does not implement. /proc/cpuinfo lists fp asimd aes pmull sha1 sha2 crc32 atomics fphp asimdhp jscvt fcma lrcpc sha3 sm3 sm4 asimddp sha512 asimdfhm dit uscat flagm sb paca pacg i8mm bf16 bti -- and no SVE. Setting HNSWLIB_NO_NATIVE=1 fixes it completely.
1_hnswlib_builds_under_termux.functional_check: With HNSWLIB_NO_NATIVE=1: import OK; add_items and knn_query run; self-recall@5 = 1.0000 against brute force over 2,000 random 16-d vectors; 11.4 us per query; and l2 returns SQUARED distance, matching the convention this project's index code depends on (ADR-0018).
1_hnswlib_builds_under_termux.why_the_functional_check_mattered: This pre-declaration required 'a functional knn_query check rather than just an import', and that requirement is the only reason this was caught. A build-exit-code check reports PASS for a library that SIGILLs on import. An import check would have caught it here but would not have verified the distance convention. Both builds return 0.
1_hnswlib_builds_under_termux.action_required: Any device-side build in Phase 3.5 or Phase 9 MUST set HNSWLIB_NO_NATIVE=1. This belongs in the device setup script, not in a person's memory.
1_hnswlib_builds_under_termux.version_mismatch_recorded: The device runs Python 3.14.6 with hnswlib 0.8.0; the laptop runs Python 3.12.14 with chroma-hnswlib 0.7.5 (ADR-0017). Different Python, different hnswlib distribution, different version. Index files written by one are not assumed loadable by the other, and Phase 9 must verify that rather than presume it.

2_battery_current_without_root.verdict: PASS -- measured current is available without root
2_battery_current_without_root.evidence: termux-battery-status (Termux:API 0.53.0 app + termux-api 0.59.1 package) returns a `current` field in microamps, readable with NO root. The pre-declared test was whether the value MOVES under load, because a constant or zero reading is not a usable energy source. It moves: -215000 uA at idle against -104000 uA with two busy loops running, at 35.0 C and 35.1 C respectively. Voltage also tracked, 4331 -> 4311 mV. The direction is physically consistent -- the handset was charging, so a larger SoC draw leaves less current reaching the battery.
2_battery_current_without_root.why_it_matters: The more dangerous of the two. If /sys/class/power_supply/battery/current_now is absent or denied AND Termux:API's current field is unavailable or does not move under load, there is NO measured energy anywhere in this project. Phase 3's energy MAPE criterion would then be unachievable as scoped, not merely hard, and the project's claims must shrink to latency-only BEFORE Phase 4 fits anything.
2_battery_current_without_root.unblock: Section 2 of the probe reads the sysfs nodes, calls termux-battery-status, and takes two current readings 10 s of CPU load apart. A value identical or zero across both reads is not a usable energy source.
2_battery_current_without_root.remaining_route: Termux:API's `termux-battery-status`, which reads BatteryManager.BATTERY_PROPERTY_CURRENT_NOW through the Android API rather than sysfs and is therefore not subject to the SELinux denial. It needs the Termux app AND the separate Termux:API app. If that also returns no current, or a value that does not move under load, there is no measured energy anywhere in this project and C4's energy half and C5 must be rescoped rather than postponed.
2_battery_current_without_root.blocker_for_measurement: WiFi is disabled on the handset and it is on mobile data (rmnet_data4 192.0.0.2), so wireless adb could not be established and the phone cannot be unplugged while staying reachable. Discharge current cannot be measured over a USB cable that is charging the battery.
2_battery_current_without_root.caveat: Both readings were taken while PLUGGED_AC, because USB adb was the only transport at the time. Charging current is not discharge current, and Phase 3.5's trace must be taken unplugged over wireless adb (172.16.23.203:5555, already established). The sign convention must also be re-established when discharging rather than assumed from these two samples.
2_battery_current_without_root.sysfs_note: The sysfs route stays dead and this does not revive it: /sys/class/power_supply/battery/current_now is unreadable to the adb shell user under Android 16 SELinux. Termux:API works because it goes through BatteryManager, an Android API, rather than through the filesystem. Any code written against sysfs will fail on this device.
2_battery_current_without_root.consequence: The project's worst case does not happen. C4's energy half and C5 are NOT sunk, and Phase 3's energy criterion is achievable as scoped rather than needing to shrink to latency-only. This is the single most consequential answer in the probe.

3_cpu_cluster_topology.verdict: ANSWERED -- and it contradicts a type in types.py
3_cpu_cluster_topology.evidence: 8 cores in THREE frequency domains: cpu0-2 max 2016000 kHz, cpu3-6 max 2803200 kHz, cpu7 max 3187200 kHz. A 3+4+1 big.LITTLE+prime arrangement. Sampled instantaneous scaling_cur_freq spanned the whole range at once: cpu0 2016000 (ratio 1.00), cpu2 1228800 (0.61), cpu6 614400 (0.22), cpu7 864000 (0.27).
3_cpu_cluster_topology.why_it_matters: DeviceState.freq_ratio was specified as a single scalar, which assumes one clock domain. Real SoCs are big.LITTLE with 2-3 clusters, and the scheduler decides placement, not the code.
3_cpu_cluster_topology.unblock: Section 3 counts distinct cpuinfo_max_freq values (= cluster count) and reads which CPU a busy Python thread actually lands on. NO fix for the scalar assumption is proposed until this is measured.
3_cpu_cluster_topology.consequence: DeviceState.freq_ratio is a single scalar and this device has no single clock ratio to report. Four cores held four different ratios in one sample, and which one a query experiences depends on where the Android scheduler placed the thread -- which this project does not control and cannot observe from inside the process. NO fix is applied here: changing types.py requires the supervisor's go-ahead, and the honest options (per-cluster vector, the ratio of the core the thread actually ran on, or a documented worst-case) differ in what they would let the controller claim.

4_thermal_zones_readable.evidence: 110 thermal zones, readable by the adb shell user with no root. Live values at idle: cpuss-0..3 40.6-41.4 C, cpu-0-0..2 40.0 C (little cluster), cpu-1-0..10 38.6-41.8 C (big/prime), gpuss-0..4 35.8-37.0 C, skin-msm-therm 32.7 C, battery 31.0 C, vir_amb 25.1 C.
4_thermal_zones_readable.why_it_matters: The phone is the only source of thermal ground truth in this project (ADR-0007, ADR-0008).
4_thermal_zones_readable.unblock: Section 4 enumerates every zone with its type and temp. Which zone is the SoC package is a device-specific AMBIGUITY to record, not a mapping to guess.
4_thermal_zones_readable.trap_recorded: 21 of the 110 zones report -273000 (= -273 C, absolute zero), which is a disabled or absent sensor rather than a reading. Any aggregate that averages or minimises over all zones without filtering these will be wrong, and wrong in a direction that looks like a cold device.
4_thermal_zones_readable.ambiguity_recorded: There is no single 'SoC package' zone to map to DeviceState.temperature_c. There are 4 cpuss, 14 cpu-*, and 5 gpuss sensors disagreeing by up to 3.2 C at idle. Which to use is a device-specific choice to be declared and justified, not guessed -- as this pre-declaration required.

5_termux_survives_sustained_load.verdict: PASS at 150 s -- not yet evidence for 30 minutes
5_termux_survives_sustained_load.evidence: termux-wake-lock acquired successfully. A CPU-bound Python child ran under it and was confirmed ALIVE at t=30, 60, 90 and 120 s. At t=150 s the liveness probe reported DEAD, which is the child COMPLETING its 150 s of scheduled work rather than being killed: `final child exit=0`, where an Android kill would have surfaced as 137. Recorded because the liveness check alone cannot distinguish 'finished' from 'killed' at the boundary, and only the exit code disambiguates it.
5_termux_survives_sustained_load.why_it_matters: Android's OOM killer and battery optimisation target exactly this kind of long-running background process. Phase 3.5 needs 30 minutes.
5_termux_survives_sustained_load.unblock: Section 5 is a 2-minute smoke test with a wake-lock held, checking liveness every 30 s, and notes whether termux-wake-lock needed Termux:API.
5_termux_survives_sustained_load.limits: This is the 2-minute smoke test this pre-declaration asked for, and it is NOT evidence for the 30-minute trace Phase 3.5 needs. It also spawned ONE child process, while Android 12+'s phantom process killer targets apps exceeding a child-process limit -- a compile or a multi-process benchmark is a different test from a single busy loop, and Termux 0.118.3 dates from 2022 while this handset runs Android 16.
5_termux_survives_sustained_load.thermal_signal_observed: Battery temperature rose monotonically under load across the run: 36.2 -> 36.4 -> 36.6 -> 36.9 C. Small, but real and measurable, which is direct evidence that the thermal ground truth Phase 4 needs is obtainable from this device.

6_llama_cpp_python_wheel.evidence: uv pip install --only-binary=:all: --dry-run llama-cpp-python on CPython 3.12.14 / win-amd64: 'Because all versions of llama-cpp-python have no usable wheels and you require llama-cpp-python, we can conclude that your requirements are unsatisfiable.' Allowing source builds resolves llama-cpp-python==0.3.35 plus diskcache==5.6.3.
6_llama_cpp_python_wheel.conclusion: No binary wheel exists for ANY version on this platform and Python. Phase 7 requires the MSVC C++ Build Tools, exactly as hnswlib did before ADR-0017 -- and unlike hnswlib there is no differently-named redistribution to fall back on. Phase 7 is gated on a toolchain install that needs elevation.
6_llama_cpp_python_wheel.note: This check had been deferred twice. It takes under a minute and the answer is unambiguous.
6_llama_cpp_python_wheel.superseded_by: ADR-0043. The wheel finding is correct and unchanged; the CONCLUSION drawn from it -- that Phase 7 is gated on MSVC -- was wrong. Phase 7 needs a generator, not llama.cpp, and transformers has been installed since Phase 1. Phase 7 is complete.

7_experimental_controls.evidence: Captured automatically: plugged state PLUGGED_AC, status CHARGING, battery level 92-93%, battery temperature 35.0-36.9 C, virtual ambient 25.1 C, battery technology Li-poly, health GOOD, cycle count 1157.
7_experimental_controls.why_it_matters: Phase 3.5's 30-minute trace and Phase 9's validation runs are only comparable to each other if charging state, state-of-charge, ambient conditions and physical setup are fixed and matching. A phone on a bed throttles differently from one on a desk. Recording the baseline now costs nothing; discovering the mismatch after both traces exist costs a redo.
7_experimental_controls.unblock: Section 7 records charging state, percentage and battery temperature automatically; ambient temperature and physical setup must be written down by hand.
7_experimental_controls.control_violation_recorded: The handset was CHARGING throughout every measurement in this probe. That is a control violation for energy and must not be repeated in the Phase 3.5 trace. Wireless adb is already established at 172.16.23.203:5555 precisely so the cable can be removed.
7_experimental_controls.sign_convention_warning: The `current` field's SIGN is not stable while charging: across the Q5 run it read -106000, +110000, +46000, +97000 uA at 30-second intervals under continuous load. Magnitude responds to load, but the sign flips as the charger modulates. Any energy integration written against these samples would be wrong. The convention MUST be re-established from an unplugged, discharging device before a single joule is reported.
still_by_hand: physical setup (desk, not bed or pocket)

phase_3_5_decision: GO, with two required conditions. All seven questions are answered and both critical ones passed: hnswlib runs on-device (Q1, with HNSWLIB_NO_NATIVE=1 mandatory) and measured battery current is available without root and moves under load (Q2). The project's worst case -- no measured energy anywhere -- does not happen, so C4's energy half and C5 stay in scope rather than being rescoped away. CONDITION 1: the trace must be taken UNPLUGGED over wireless adb, because every reading here was taken while charging and the current sign is unstable in that state. CONDITION 2: Q5 passed at 150 seconds with one child process; the 30-minute multi-process case is untested, and Termux 0.118.3 predates this handset's Android 16 by four major versions.
what_is_already_certain: hnswlib builds AND runs on this device, but ONLY with HNSWLIB_NO_NATIVE=1; the default build succeeds and then SIGILLs on import (Q1).
Measured battery current is available without root via Termux:API and responds to load (Q2). There IS a measured energy path in this project.
Thermal ground truth is available without root, from 110 zones, and rises measurably under load (Q4, Q5).
The sysfs battery route is dead under Android 16 SELinux; only the BatteryManager API works (Q2).
DeviceState.freq_ratio's single-scalar assumption does not hold on this 3-cluster SoC (Q3). Unresolved pending a decision on types.py.
This development machine remains incapable of measuring temperature or energy (ADR-0007, ADR-0008); the phone is the only source.
